title: Microfeature runway — seedlog for compact response lanes
content:
Context and purpose:

Quick personal seedlog for a small product experiment: lightweight ‘compact response lanes’ that dynamically pick a response fidelity profile per request. Not a full PRD — this is a scratchpad with rough user stories, goals, constraints, and quick rollout paths. Use to scope an MVP for Q4 micro-release and hand to an engineer for feasibility spike.

Problem statement (very short):
- Many customers want predictable per-turn cost with bounded latency for chat features.
- Current knobset (model selection, token limits, batching) is too coarse and expensive for small tweaks.
- We can expose a higher-level microfeature: lane presets that map to combined runtime policies (model variant, quantization profile, prefix caching policy, response length cap, token sampling seeds).

Hypothesis:
- If we provide 3 opinionated compact lanes (concise, balanced, rich) and an auto mode, teams will reduce per-message token usage by ~25% on average for casual assistant flows while maintaining >90% user satisfaction.

Goals / success metrics (MVP):
- Primary: 20–30% reduction in tokens-per-interaction for targeted flows (FAQ, short replies) after 4 weeks.
- Latency: median delta vs baseline < +40ms for concision lane; p95 < +120ms.
- Reliability: no new error class introduced; fallback to baseline model on failure.
- Adoption: opt-in from 3 pilot customers / internal apps in 6 weeks.

User stories (rough, prioritized):
1) As a product engineer, I want to annotate an API route with a lane name so the runtime applies the lane policy automatically. Acceptance: route-level config + API header allow lane override.
2) As an app developer, I want an 'auto' mode that chooses concision for short-turn intents (detected heuristically) so I don't manually tag all routes. Acceptance: toggle in console + simple heuristics rule set.
3) As an SRE, I want telemetry bounded per-lane (tokens, latency, fallback rate) so we can evaluate economic impact. Acceptance: new metrics exposed in console and metric tags in traces.
4) As a customer-facing PM, I want a way to preview differences locally (delta tokens, sample responses) to sign off on quality. Acceptance: preview page in console + CLI shim.

MVP lane definitions (initial draft):
- concision: small model variant (e.g., 7B-quantized), aggressive length cap (max 60 tokens), sampling tuned for brevity, use prefix-KV caching when possible. Fallback: balanced lane.
- balanced: default production settings.
- rich: higher-capacity model, relaxed caps, sampling for richness. Fallback: balanced.
- auto: runtime selects concision vs balanced based on intent-length heuristic + simple signal (user message length < 120 chars => concision).

Runtime constraints / non-goals:
- This is not a model training or RL loop. No online fine-tuning.
- Avoid adding heavy new routing churn; lanes should map to existing model variants where possible.
- Not aiming to replace explicit model selection features for power users.

Observability plan (light):
- Tag requests with lane name + effective model variant + fallback flag.
- Per-lane dashboards: tokens per request, avg latency, p95 latency, fallback rate, relative satisfaction proxy (if client emits feedback).
- Quick eval harness: 500 prompt samples from common FAQ/TD flows to calculate token delta and BLEU-ish similarity to baseline.

Rollout plan (sketch):
1) Spike (1 week): engineer pairs with infra to ensure lane header is plumbed end-to-end and simple config maps to runtime behavior.
2) Internal pilot (2 weeks): enable for internal assistant + docs bot, collect metrics and eyeball responses.
3) Beta customer pilot (4 weeks): opt-in flag for 2 customers. Monitor.
4) Public: expose lanes in console UI + API docs + sample presets.

Risks and mitigations:
- Quality regression: provide easy rollback per-route, and automatic fallback to balanced lane when quality metric drops.
- Unexpected cost shifts: set coarse budget guardrails per-route and per-org to prevent lane misuse.
- UX confusion: default to balanced; hide concision behind an explicit opt-in for new users.

Quick UI ideas (console):
- Route config pane: dropdown 'response lane' with preview button.
- Preview modal shows side-by-side sample outputs and token estimate.
- Metrics card: lane delta vs baseline (tokens, latency).

Open questions / things to spike in the feasibility phase:
- What are the smallest quantized model variants we can safely route to without SDK/serving changes? (ping infra + serving-runtime)
- Can we enforce per-response token caps reliably across streaming APIs and function-calls?
- How to instrument a robust quality signal for automatic switching in 'auto' mode? (heuristics vs cheap client-side feedback)
- What cost dashboard granularity do customers need (per-lane, per-route, per-user)?

Next steps (to-do list):
- [ ] Schedule 2-hour spike with infra (Elliot) to validate header plumbing and model variant mapping.
- [ ] Create small eval set (Mira) focused on short-turn assistant prompts.
- [ ] Draft minimal console wireframe for preview + route dropdown (product mock).
- [ ] Draft safety fallback policy: threshold values for automatic re-route to balanced.

Notes to self / rough ideas: keep lanes lightweight and opinionated. Focus on a small win (FAQ + short assistant replies). If concision wins, consider expanding 'economy' lane family (more aggressive cost profile) later.

References / links:
- CONFLUENCE-8823: compact-response-features brainstorm (seed doc)
- JIRA-INF-1198: runtime header plumbing spike
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/432 (preview panel prototype)
summary: Seedlog for a microfeature: compact response lanes. Draft user stories, goals, MVP lane definitions, rollout sketch, and open questions.
